hints: Interpret $|z-2i|\leq|z+2-i|$ as points at least as close to $2i$ as to $-2+i$.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $(0,2)$ and $(-2,1)$, then keep the side containing $(0,2)$; include the boundary.
Interpret $0\leq\arg(z+1)\leq\frac{\pi}{4}$ as the sector from $(-1,0)$ between the positive real direction and the half-line of gradient $1$.
Shade only the intersection of that closed sector with the chosen half-plane.
walkthrough:
Interpret the first inequality $|z - 2\mathrm{i}| \leqslant |z + 2 - \mathrm{i}|$ as a distance condition:
$|z - 2\mathrm{i}| \leqslant |z - (-2 + \mathrm{i})|$ means the distance from $z$ to $(0, 2)$ is less than or equal to the distance from $z$ to $(-2, 1)$.
The boundary is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining $(-2, 1)$ and $(0, 2)$.

Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector:
$$\text{Midpoint} = \left(\dfrac{-2 + 0}{2}, \dfrac{1 + 2}{2}\right) = \left(-1, \dfrac{3}{2}\right)$$
$$\text{Segment gradient} = \dfrac{2 - 1}{0 - (-2)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$\text{Perpendicular gradient} = -2$$
$$y - \dfrac{3}{2} = -2(x - (-1)) \implies y = -2x - \dfrac{1}{2}$$

Identify the half-plane satisfying $|z - 2\mathrm{i}| \leqslant |z + 2 - \mathrm{i}|$:
Points closer to $(0, 2)$ lie on or above/to the right of the line $y = -2x - \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Interpret the second condition $0 \leqslant \arg(z + 1) \leqslant \dfrac{1}{4}\pi$:
$z + 1 = z - (-1)$, so this represents a wedge emanating from $(-1, 0)$.
The lower ray is the horizontal half-line $y = 0$ for $x \geqslant -1$ (argument $0$).
The upper ray is the half-line of gradient $1$ starting at $(-1, 0)$, passing through $(0, 1)$ (argument $\pi/4$).

Shade the region of intersection:
Shade the region lying inside the angular sector between the rays from $(-1, 0)$ and on or above the perpendicular bisector line, including the solid boundaries.

ai_rubric.Argand Loci: Demonstrates the points representing $2i$ and $-2+i$. Demonstrates the half-line of gradient $1$ from $(-1,0)$. Concludes that intersection of the half-plane on the $2i$ side of the perpendicular bisector of $2i$ and $-2+i$ with the sector from $-1$ between arguments $0$ and $\pi/4$.
